July, 1995          Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 W.A. Yates...........03    06

 Keith Taylor.........18    20

 Fred Ridout..........23    26

 Keith Taylor.........32    33

 Bertie Robert........38    40

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From W.A. Yates, CHORLEY



Dear Brian,


In April 1994,OUTLET 80,you very
kindly sorted out a program
called FOLIO (which is intended
to keep track of stocks and
shares) by altering the OPEN and
CLOSE statements.


This worked fine in as much that
I could save on to disk and SNAP
print but I eventually realised
that there should be more to the
program and I have now managed
to get hold of the rest of it.


You get a menu on the screen
from which you can print out any
of five choices (Portfolio)...
Valuation,Performance, Analysis,
Income Summary and Transaction
Summary.

It does a print out but it does
not come out as it should. Under
PRICE it prints :- 0.00 with the
real price underneath, and under
YIELD again it prints 0.0% with
the real yield underneath.


I would also, if possible, like
to be able to get a print out
wider than 32 lines - say, 50 or
thereabouts and centralised.  I
shall be very pleased if you can
advise me as to how to do it.


I am enclosing a copy on disk.

Hoping you can help - there does
not seem to be much that you
can't sort out!

               All best wishes

               yours sincerely,

                  W.A. Yates

Brian Cavers to W.A. Yates

Yes,  it can be done but it will
need quite a lot of tedious work
to rewrite scores of lines! I'll
describe what you need to do but
recommend you do it a stage at a
time and keep saving the program
as separate copies. Keep a note
of exactly what you have done
and which line number you have
reached and check the results as
you go. Then, if anything goes
wrong you can just go back to
the last copy and not have to go
right back and start all over
again! Here goes...

First, the easy bit - centralis-
ing the printout. For this you
need some printer codes...


The program starts at line 10 so
add some new lines...

20 POKE @6,1
30 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"l";CHR$ 24;

80 POKE @6,0

Make sure you get every detail,
even the semi-colon at the end.
The POKE @6,1 enables the Plus D
or Disciple to send printer con-
trol codes; POKE @6,0 lets you
LLIST a BASIC program and print
normal text such as your program
and it automatically starts a
new line after every LPRINT,that
is, UNLESS you add a semi-colon
to the text or numbers being
printed, eg, LPRINT 99; in which
case it stops on the same line.


The CHR$(27) in line 30 means a
printer control code follows.The
small "l" means left margin and
CHR$(24) is the number of char-
acter spaces in the left margin.
To centre 32 characters on an 80
column printer you need a 24
column margin at left and right.

However, you prefer the printout
to be wider than 32 and this may
not be so easy. You can either
adjust all the variables through
the program (which I'll describe
later in brief) or consider the
alternatives which may satisfy
you...

You might like wide print.Try...

40 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"W1";


Note that the "W1" has the digit
"one" and not a small "l" and
also note that your text will
not now be centralised.Wide text
of 32 characters is the width of
64 normal characters so alter
the left margin from 24 to 8.

Your printer may also be able to
do double height. I don't have a
printer with this feature but I
understand the codes are...

LPRINT CHR$ 27;CHR$ 126;CHR$ 1;

If you don't like wide print it
may be possible to alter the
pitch instead with CHR$ 27;CHR$
126;"3";CHR$ n; ...where n is a
number from 0 to 7 but I do not
know much about this.


Anyway,any codes you want to try
from your printer manual such as
emphasised or double-strike can
be entered between those line 20
to 80.

Now,the "0.00" is printed by the
program as dozens and dozens of
separate commands! The structure
is something like this...

The program calculates the value
to be printed in a variable x1.

It first PRINTS/LPRINTS "0.00".

It GO SUBs 3670 to calculate the
place on a line to print the
value of x1 (so it is lined up).
It puts this in variable xpc and
x1 into the string x$.


It then returns from the GO SUB
and PRINTs and LPRINTS x$. The
screen PRINT is OK because it
OVERPRINTS the "0.00" but the +D
PRINT AT is really only like a
TAB and cannot go backwards so
it has to go to the next line!
Even if it could, of course, it
would not obliterate the orig-
inal like on the screen but it
would print on top of the 0.00
so you would get a mess!

I assume the "0.00" is printed
to cover cases where only "0"
would be printed or say, 55
would then print over the first
0 to show 55.00. It is a crude
way of formatting the values and
unfortunately some values use it
and some don't!


The program needs extensive re-
writing really so the best I can
come up with is first create an
ADDITIONAL GO SUB...

6670 LET x$=STR$ x1

6690 IF x1=INT x1 THEN LET
     x$=x$+"."

6700 LET x$=x$+"00"

6710 IF x$=(LEN x$-2)<> "." THEN
     LET x$=x$(TO LEN x$-1):
     GO TO 6710

6720 LET xpc=xpc-LEN x$ + 3

6750 IF xpc<0 THEN LET xpc=0

6770 RETURN


Now work slowly and carefully
through the program...

1. REMOVE ALL commands to PRINT
   and LPRINT "0.00"

2. ALTER the associated GO SUB
   3670 to GO SUB 6670. Do NOT
   alter EVERY GO SUB 3670 in
   the program but ONLY the ones
   that closely follow a "0.00".

3. REMOVE any LET x$=STR$ x1 in
   any of such lines.

Where the value is a percentage
it is intended to be only to one
decimal place but I'd live with
that if I were you as it makes
it less complex to alter and I
think it looks OK.


I recommend you do one section
at a time. If you start at line
2110 you will see the heading...
"Portfolio Valuation" which
starts that section. The first
line to alter in the section is:

2170 PRINT AT qpc,9;"0.00": LET
     x1=INT(p(gpc)*100+0.5)/100:
     LET xpc=4: GO SUB 3670:
     PRINT AT qpc, 6+xpc;x$;

      Alter to...
2170                         LET
     x1=INT(p(gpc)*100+0.5)/100:
     LET xpc=4: GO SUB 6670:
     PRINT AT qpc, 6+xpc;x$;

I show it spaced out above for
clarity so you can see the first
part is gone and the GO SUB
changed.

Line 2175 follows it...

2175 LPRINT AT qpc,9;"0.00";AT
     qpc,6+xpc;x$;

Alter it to...

2175 LPRINT AT qpc,6+xpc;x$;

Alter all the similar lines in
that section. All the sections
will end with a RETURN - in this
case it is at line 2270. Save a
new copy of the program before
you test it and later any more.

Note that where there is a per-
centage value, eg, PRINT "0.00%"
delete that as usual but alter
the PRINT x$; and the LPRINT x$;
to X$;"%";


Take great care with every dot
and comma and it should work. I
cannot guarantee though that
there is something I have not
spotted which may go wrong!

To space the text out more you
need to alter the value of xpc
as defined in each calc line, eg
in line 2170 it is xpc=4. If you
alter that to xpc=6 or 7 it will
probably work. Of course, you'll
have to alter ALL the lines in
that section. Do not just add a
fixed amount like 2 or 3; add
say, a third of the original. It
should then space out more. You
must do this not only for the
lines you have already altered
but ALL the lines that declare
xpc and then PRINT!!


You might first try adding to
both GO SUB 3670 and 6670 (near
the start before xpc is changed)
LET xpc=xpc+xpc/3 (or xpc/2 etc)
but I can't guarantee this will
work perfectly. Perhaps...
xpc=INT(xpc+xpc/3) might be
better. Experiment!

I have kept a copy of the disk
and a printed listing for ref-
erence temporarily so if any
specific thing crops up let me
know and I will try to help a
bit more.
                     Brian

From : Keith Taylor, OLDHAM

(1). I have a number Of programs
on disk that I have created for
my own use but to load them I
would like to use loader and not
load ""

(2). One program I have on tape
is causing me a bit of a head-
ache, it's called "Bizzicom" by
Merlin Software (heard of it ?).
My problem is that although I've
managed to transfer it to disk
using a Multiface 3, any changes
made to it have to go to tape or
microdrive! Could you or someone
out in Speccyland please advise
me how to save the changes to
disc (if pos.) I've tried saving
the changes to tape but it won't
load.

(3). I have a Speccy +3 that I
bought on the market. The comp-
uter works fine but when I load
a disk, the message: "drive not
ready" comes up. There seems to
be no power reaching the drive.
From the same stall I bought a
Multiface 3.  I wonder if the
drive has just been turned off
through an internal command or
perhaps because an external
drive may have been used. Any
ideas?

                  Keith Taylor

Brian Cavers to Keith Taylor

1. To load a program from +3
   disk direct from the menu
loader name it with the filename
"DISK". For example, suppose you
have a program called "GERONIMO"
that, in turn, loads a SCREEN$
file called "GERONIMO.PIC" and
a code file "GERONIMO.BIN" then
rename the main program by typ-
ing in BASIC(no line number)...

   MOVE "GERONIMO" TO "DISK"

Alternatively,write a program...

  10 LOAD "GERONIMO"
             and save it with...

    SAVE "DISK" LINE 10


2. I do not know the program you
mentioned called "BIZZICOM". If
you make any changes to it then
re-run it then save the new
version to disk by pressing the
Multiface button just as if you
had just loaded it from tape.If,
by "any changes made to it" you
mean data saved from it then it
sounds like it is saved by a
machine code routine because if
the BASIC tape SAVE syntax were
used it would save to disk any-
way. Therefore,only someone very
experienced in machine code and
with plenty of time to spare is
likely to be able to change the
program.

Let me have more information on
what exactly you are saving and
by what means.

3. The +3 drive sounds dodgy. If
you have OUTLET 66 then read Ray
Barnes' letter about the drive
belt.If you open it up you might
check if there are any obvious
connections loose, etc.You might
strike lucky and it sounds like
you have nothing to lose.

                       Brian

From Fred Ridout, SWINDON

Dear Eds,

I have Three or four questions I
would like answered about the +3
if you would be so kind and they
are:-

1.I have a LLIST problem.  I can
print up to about 60 lines and
then it stops with 8 END OF FILE
- an error not covered in the
book.  After this it will only
LLIST one line before being
stopped by error 8 again.Also it
will not LLIST from a line i.e.
LLIST 200.  This applies both to
an entered LLIST and the MENU. I
have two +3s and the result is
the same on both.


2. I would like to have the CAT
printed on the screen across,ie,
two columns so as to get more on
before it scrolls - like used in
TASWORD +3.


3. On my monitor I cannot get
BRIGHT. This does not worry me
except that MASTERFILE +3 uses
BRIGHT to highlight the CAT list
and others. Is there a POKE that
can substitute a colour bar in-
stead of bright?



4. I see that some of your list-
ings in OUTLET include a +3 POKE
and +3 print bug.What are these?



Now for something different.  I
copied out a program from YOUR
COMPUTER March 85 by Jon Ellis
called SECURIFILE  and I have
been using it ever since in
various forms. In all this time
it has never crashed on me.  I
did get JON to put a single step
view in it. As I now use a +3,is
it possible to alter the LOAD/
SAVE routine to suit disc opera-
tion;also the printer routine? I
alter the font with on screen
UT1 to suit whatever characters
I require.  I think the printer
must print graphics only.

  Hoping I can twist your arm,

            Yours,
                    Fred

Brian Cavers to Fred Ridout

1. This LLIST problem sounds
like it may simply be codes in
the particular program you are
trying to LLIST. Am I right in
thinking that you have just come
across it in one program? Look
at the last line printed or the
one just after. Are there any
colour codes or other codes in
the line? Is it a REM line with
machine code hidden in it? Try
modifying or deleting that one
line and then LLIST it.  If all
else fails the only other thing
I can think of is to split the
program in two while you LLIST
it in two separate parts.  Use
LEAVER from OUTLET 79 to split
it in two or three pieces.


2. There is no simple +3 command
to get the CAT printed in two
columns like on the +D. So, I've
written some code to do it for
you and this will appear in a
future OUTLET soon I hope.  It
not only prints the CAT in two
columns but you can change it to
print as many filenames as will
fit on a line.  It uses wordwrap
so filenames are not split over
the end of the line and the
start of the next and you have a
choice of dividing characters to
make it clearer. For example,the
filenames can be separated by
just a space or by a star or by
a solid block character.  Mean-
while you might look at CATDB in
OUTLET 76,CATLOADER in OUTLET 33
or print the CAT with CAT #3.


3. There is no simple software
solution to getting BRIGHT on a
monitor that does not provide it
I'm afraid. Ray Barnes described
a hardware fix in OUTLETTERS in
OUTLET 66.  However if you just
want a POKE for MASTERFILE +3
then let me see...

MF+3 does not use code files. It
reads its files direct using
machine code. This is not avail-
able from BASIC.  There is a +3
disk editor in OUTLET 51 called
EDIS but this only shows text. I
will have a look at it and see
if I can modify it to show the
actual values.  I should then be
able to scan the disk for the
BRIGHT codes 18,1 and, if found,
alter them to say, INVERSE.


I have made a note to try this
when I have time but I cannot
guarantee that it will work.
Watch this space.

4. Normally, if you use the +3
menu loader to load a program
that auto-runs,  if there is an
error or you press BREAK then if
you press ENTER to see the list-
ing the +3 automatically exits
back to the menu loader!  This
makes it difficult to find a bug
or examine a program. The POKE+3
at line 1001 in the OUTLET'DISK'
file switches this off.

Some +3s have a printer bug that
prevents any printing I believe
(my +3 is OK). The line at 1002
fixes this.


I do not think that line 1002
will solve your LLIST problem
but you could try it.  Just load
any recent OUTLET,  load a pro-
gram then press BREAK and enter
LOAD "NAME" to load the program
you want to LLIST.  Don't BREAK
into the CONTENTS program as the
character set is corrupted (yet
another +3 design flaw). Nearly
all OUTLET programs have a fix
for this at line 9900 but there
is not room in CONTENTS.

Finally, the SECURIFILE program
is entirely machine code and it
would be a huge task to edit it.
We always recommend that progr-
ammers put LOAD,SAVE and printer
commands in BASIC for this very
reason!


The job could take me two weeks
full-time.  I would be prepared
to tackle the job for a charge
of `500 which is a fair price
for 10 days skilled work! But, I
would have to spread the 10 days
over several months because of
other work I have to do!Further,
I could not guarantee success!

If the programmer had put the
commands in BASIC I could do it
in two minutes and wouldn't have
to charge you anything!

If any other reader would like a
challenge and is experienced in
machine code then please volunt-
eer!
                      Brian.

From Keith Taylor, OLDHAM

Thank you for sending me the
'Clipper 1' compilation disk but
I'm a little disappointed that I
can't get it to print out indiv-
idual boxes - only full pages.

Can you please tell me if either
I am doing something wrong or do
I need a compiler disk for it?

            Keith Taylor


Brian Cavers to Keith Taylor

CLIP COMPOSER, which is included
on the CLIPPER 1 disk, has a lot
of different features so takes a
while to get the hang of it all.
You can actually compose screens
made up of multiple images taken
from any Spectrum screen so to
print a single clip art image it
is simply a matter of composing
a screen with that one image and
then printing that.Here's how to
do it in a step-by-step example
for clarity...

 1.Load Clipper 1
 2.Pick Option 4 to see screens
 3.Select an image to print.
 4.Note down the screen number
  shown at bottom centre)


 5.Press E to exit
 6.Press 1 for Clip Composer
 7.Press R to run it
 8.Press L to load a screen
 9.Enter the filename which is
   CLIP2.n where n is the one
   you picked. For example, say
   you pick the little tree at
   the top right of Screen 2.
   You now enter CLIP2.2
10.Enter the drive
11.Enter S for screen
12.You should now see the screen
13.Press the up arrow key and a
   flashing box in the middle is
   moved up. Use the arrow keys
   to move it to the top left of
   the tree image
14.Press B to get BOX SIZE
15.Move the down and right arrow
   keys to enlarge the box to
   surround the tree

16.Press G to 'GET' the tree
17.Press A to Z (say T for tree)
18.Press B twice to get BOX MOVE
18.Move the box to the extreme
   top left of the screen
19.Press B to get BOX SIZE
20.Use down and right arrows to
   enlarge the box to fill the
   entire screen
21.Press G to 'GET'
22.Press SHIFT and A together to
   clear the screen
23.Use the up and left arrow key
   to shrink the box right down
24.Press B twice for BOX MOVE
25.Move the box to about centre
26.Press P to 'PUT'
27.Press T for the tree
28.You should now have a screen
   with just the tree on it in
   the middle somewhere


29.Remove the Clipper disk and
   put a disk with some spare
   room in the drive
30.Press S to SAVE
31.Enter CLIP2.1 as filename
32.Enter drive
33.Enter S for screen
34.After it has saved remove the
   disk and replace the Clipper
   disk
35.Press Q to quit
36.Press B to boot
37.Remove the Clipper disk and
   put the disk with the tree
   screen back in the drive
38.Press 4 to view screens
39.The tree picture should show
40.Press P to print
41.Curse the printer because you
   find you've run out of paper
42.Have a cup of tea instead


Instead of loading the tree back
into Clipper it might be easier
to save it with a more sensible
name like TREE.S on a spare disk
and then create a little program
of your own to print it thus...

10 LOAD "TREE.S" SCREEN$
20 COPY     (or COPY EXP)

The foregoing instructions may
sound lengthy when listed with
every dot and comma but once you
get the hang of it you can do
endless permutations to make up
all kinds of screens. You might
also look at CLIPSTICK in OUTLET
85 which is an improved version
of CLIP COMPOSER by a reader.
Let me know if you need any more
help.
                          Brian

From: R.A. Roberts, BELFAST

Dear Brian,

Here's a ribbon-saving tip.Norm-
ally I use "Re-Ink" from Caspell
Computer, FREEPOST,Poole,Dorset,
BH15 2BR (Tel: 01202 66615, Fax:
01202 668208).  This really ext-
ends the life of printer ribbons
BUT, as I have been in the "pay"
of the "SS"(unemployed) for four
years,I cannot really afford it!

The solution, given to me by a
friend some time ago, is WD40!
Printer ribbons are only "hit"
by the print head in the middle
(width-wise) - with the result
that there is plenty of ink left
at the top and bottom edges.


What the WD40 does is re-distri-
bute the unused ink from the
edges over the whole ribbon and
thus restore the printability of
the ribbon. The ribbon used for
this letter has been so treated,
and, as you can see, gives very
good results.

         All the best,

        Bertie Roberts

Brian Cavers to Bertie Roberts

An excellent tip and I might try
that myself soon. Anyone who has
never used a re-ink spray might
wonder how you apply it. Ribbon
cases usually can be popped open
along their central seam with a
fine screwdriver or knife and
the ribbon is curled up inside.

Needless to say, you have to
take care not spill it out and
put it on thick newspaper or
something while you do it! The
case can be popped back together
again after and then the ribbon
wound through manually a little
bit just to make sure it is not
trapped anywhere and can move
smoothly.


I suppose instead one might just
drip the WD40 on the ribbon that
is exposed and keep winding it
through.How practical that would
be I don't know!

Whichever method is used,I guess
it might help to leave it for an
hour or so to soak in before use
to give the ink a chance to move
across - or does the WD40 act
immediately?

                         Brian.
